== The World is a Stage ==


-- Story Background --

You were once a respected stage magician, known for your incredible skills in hypnosis, sleight of hand, and captivating stage presence. However, your life took a dark turn when a venue refused to pay you after a performance. Feeling wronged and desperate, you decided to use your talents for more nefarious purposes, embarking on a thrilling life of crime.


-- Character --

Name
----
Victor Ashecroft

Background
----------
A charismatic stage magician nicknamed "the Maestro of Mystery", Victor Ashecroft uses their incredible skills in hypnosis, sleight of hand, and showmanship to commit daring heists and evade capture. Their hypnotic abilities allow him to control the minds of his enemies, turning them into his loyal assistants.

Skills
------
Gadgetry: 4 (Highly skilled)
Hypnosis: 5 (Exceptional)
Stage Presence: 5 (Exceptional)
Escape Artistry: 3 (Competent)
Sleight of Hand: 4 (Highly skilled)


-- Turn 1 --

Outcome
-------
The Grandview Theater looms before you in the darkness, its art deco façade bathed in the orange glow of streetlights. Three weeks ago, they promised you five thousand dollars for your evening performance. Three weeks ago, the manager—that weasel Gerald Hutchins—claimed the box office receipts were 'disappointing' and offered you half. When you refused, he offered nothing.

You approach from the alley, where the stage door sits beneath a rusted fire escape. Your sonic wand hums softly as you hold it to the lock, its vibrations picking the mechanism in seconds. The door swings open with barely a whisper.

Inside, emergency lighting casts everything in a sickly green. You know this place intimately—the narrow corridor past the dressing rooms, the backstage area with its musty velvet curtains, and beyond that, the route to the administrative offices where Hutchins keeps his safe.

You're halfway down the corridor when you hear it: footsteps. Light, purposeful, coming from the direction of the stage.

"I know someone's here," calls a female voice, young and confident. "The motion sensors picked you up the moment you entered."

You freeze. Motion sensors? The theater didn't have those three weeks ago.

A figure emerges from the shadows ahead, stepping into a pool of emergency light. She's a woman in her mid-twenties, athletic build, wearing what can only be described as a superhero costume—a fitted navy blue bodysuit with silver accents running down the sides, silver boots that come up to mid-calf, and silver bracers on her forearms. Her dark brown hair is pulled back in a high ponytail, and her brown eyes study you with an intensity that suggests she's already analyzing your next three moves. A silver lightning bolt emblem adorns her chest.

"Victor Ashecroft," she says, and there's recognition in her voice. "The Maestro of Mystery himself. I saw your show at the Paramount last year—you were brilliant. So this is what you've turned to?"

"And you are?" you ask, your hand moving subtly toward your pocket where you keep your hypnotic light wand.

"Voltage," she replies, and small arcs of electricity dance between her fingertips as if to demonstrate. "Member of the Justice Guardians. We've been monitoring this place since Hutchins reported threats against his business. He mentioned a disgruntled performer." She takes a step closer. "I really hoped it wouldn't be you. But here we are."

The corridor is narrow, limiting her mobility but also limiting yours. Behind you is the exit. Ahead, past Voltage, lies Hutchins' office and your money.

- - - - -

Your objective for this adventure is: To use your skills in hypnosis, sleight of hand, and stage presence, to execute a series of daring heists, turn the superheroines trying to stop you into hypnotized assistants, and become a notorious supervillain.

- - - - -

Secret Information
------------------
Voltage's real name is Maya Chen. She's 24 years old, graduated top of her class in electrical engineering before a lab accident gave her electrokinetic powers. She's been with the Justice Guardians for only six months and is still somewhat idealistic about heroism. She genuinely admired Victor's stage work and is conflicted about having to stop him. Gerald Hutchins did indeed contact the Justice Guardians after receiving anonymous threatening letters (which Victor did not send—Hutchins is paranoid). Voltage is alone on this patrol; the other Guardians are dealing with incidents elsewhere in the city. She's confident but inexperienced in actual combat situations.

Voltage


-- Turn 2 --

Action
------
I sigh, theatrically, shaking my head. "I'm not surprised that he mentioned disgruntled performers - from what I uncovered, he's been stiffing his entertainers for months now. I had thought it was just me, but the deeper I looked, the more torn up, unpaid invoices I found. Have you noticed? No one ever a repeat performance at the Grandview - ever. No, I'm not surprised that his practice of hiring only poor entertainers who can't afford to sue when he refuses to pay them has earned him more than a few disgruntled phone calls."

Then, I look up at Voltage, catching her eye shrewdly. "What does surprise me, though, is that the Justice Guardians would assign one of their own to watch this venue on pure hearsay. What's your relationship to Gerald Hutchins that you would protect his property without even investigating the other side of the story he told you?"

Outcome
-------
Voltage's confident stance wavers slightly. The electricity dancing between her fingers flickers and dims as your words land. Her eyes narrow, not with suspicion of you, but with the first seeds of doubt about the situation she's been placed in.

"My relationship?" she says, but there's less certainty in her voice now. "I don't have one. The Justice Guardians received a formal request through proper channels. Hutchins filed a police report about threatening letters, and the department asked for our assistance given the potential for—"

She stops herself, clearly reconsidering. Her hand drops slightly, the electrical display fading entirely.

"What do you mean, torn up invoices?" Voltage takes a half-step back, giving herself thinking room. "You're saying this is about more than just your payment?"

You can see her mind working, the engineer in her processing new variables. She glances down the corridor toward where Hutchins's office would be, then back at you.

"Show me," she says abruptly. "If what you're saying is true, if there's evidence that Hutchins has been systematically defrauding performers, then this isn't a simple break-in situation. But I need to see proof, not just accusations."

She crosses her arms, the silver bracers catching the emergency lighting. "Here's what I'm thinking: you clearly broke in here tonight intending to take something. That's still illegal, regardless of whether you feel you're owed money. But if there's a pattern of fraud, that changes the context significantly."

Voltage tilts her head slightly, studying you with those sharp brown eyes. "You were always good at reading people, Ashecroft. I remember that from your show—the way you could pick someone from the audience and know exactly what to say to them. So you probably already know I'm the type who cares about getting things right, not just following orders blindly."

She gestures down the hallway. "Hutchins's office is that way, isn't it? Let's go look at these invoices you mentioned. Together. If they exist and show what you claim, then we have a conversation about how to handle this properly. If they don't..." The electricity returns to her fingertips, a gentle warning. "Then you're just a very talented performer trying to talk his way out of trouble."

She takes another step back, clearing a path past her. "Your choice, Maestro. Do we investigate your claims, or do we do this the hard way?"

Secret Information
------------------
Maya is genuinely conflicted now. Victor hit on something she already had mild concerns about—the Justice Guardians sometimes get requests from wealthy business owners that feel more like private security work than actual hero duty, and it's bothered her. She's also aware that she's young and inexperienced, and worried about being manipulated, which makes her both more cautious and more determined to verify facts. If Victor can produce real evidence of fraud, her sense of justice would compel her to act on it, potentially even against Hutchins. However, she's also keeping her guard up, aware that this could be an elaborate distraction or manipulation. She's deliberately positioned herself so she can still see both Victor and the exit, and she's keeping her powers ready to deploy.

Voltage


-- Turn 3 --

Action
------
I grimace, bitterly. "You think I didn't try going through the proper channels first? The police refused to listen to me or look at the evidence I'd collected - accused me of fabricating it to 'con a respected member of the community'."

I shake my head, as though trying to clear my thoughts, and take a deep breath to calm myself. My anger and bitterness is genuine - I did legitimately try to take it to the authorities, though they didn't laugh me out of the building so much as they told me 'sure, we'll look into it' and then never did. The 'proof' I have is just my own half of the contract, which Hutchins intentionally signed so illegibly that he can claim I forged it easily and then it's his word against mine and we both know who will come out on top there. But, what story doesn't benefit from a dash of truth and a drop of embellishment?

I look back up at Voltage, making a show of calming myself down. "Look - if you're serious about investigating this properly, and soon enough so that I can get paid before I get evicted, then I'll confess that I did break in to find something - more proof of what Hutchins has been doing. But - look, I appreciate your offer, I really do, but - you can't come with me to look through Hutchins' financial records - I can't imagine you're authorized to go digging through Hutchins' financial records any more than I am, and I... I don't want to make a new hero like you complicit in my crimes."

Outcome
-------
Your words hit their mark with precision. Voltage's expression shifts through several emotions in rapid succession—sympathy, frustration, and then a flash of anger that isn't directed at you.

"The police dismissed you?" She uncrosses her arms, her hands falling to her sides. "That's... that's exactly the kind of thing that—" She cuts herself off, jaw tightening. "I've seen it before. Friend of mine tried to report her landlord for housing violations. Landlord played golf with the deputy commissioner. Guess whose complaint got filed in the circular bin?"

She's quiet for a moment, then shakes her head firmly. "But here's where you're wrong about one thing, Ashecroft. I don't need authorization to look at evidence of a crime. If Hutchins is committing fraud, that's not 'his private financial records'—that's evidence. And if I witness evidence of criminal activity while investigating a reported break-in, I'm not only allowed to examine it, I'm obligated to."

Voltage takes a step forward, her boots clicking on the linoleum. "So stop trying to protect me from being 'complicit.' I'm a big girl, I can make my own ethical decisions, and right now my ethics are telling me that something stinks about this whole situation."

She gestures down the hallway toward the offices. "You said you have your half of the contract. Show it to me. Then we go to Hutchins's office together, and if we find evidence that matches your claims, we document it properly. Photos, notes, chain of custody—the works. Evidence that will actually hold up, not just stuff that can be dismissed."

Her brown eyes lock onto yours, and there's steel there beneath the idealism. "And yeah, maybe that means I'm bending a few rules about proper procedure. But I didn't put on this costume to be private security for con artists. I became a Guardian to help people who can't get help any other way."

She extends her hand toward you, not for a handshake, but palm up—a request. "Contract first. Let me see what we're dealing with. Then we search his office, and if what you're saying is true, I'll make sure the right people see the evidence. People who'll actually do something about it."

The electricity has completely faded from her hands now. She's committed to this course of action, her inexperience showing in her willingness to trust, her idealism overriding her caution.

"Come on, Maestro. You wanted someone to take you seriously. I'm taking you seriously. Don't waste it."

Secret Information
------------------
Maya has fully committed to investigating Victor's claims, her idealism and sense of justice overriding her training about maintaining proper boundaries with suspects. She's unaware that she's being emotionally manipulated, though she's correctly identified that the police dismissing Victor's claims would fit a pattern she's personally witnessed. Her decision to help him search Hutchins's office is technically defensible under 'investigating evidence discovered during a legal intervention,' but it's a gray area that a more experienced hero would recognize as dangerous. She's also dropped most of her defensive posture, no longer viewing Victor as an immediate threat. This makes her more vulnerable to hypnotic suggestion if Victor chooses to attempt it.

Voltage


-- Turn 4 --

Action
------
I look at her in surprise - genuine surprise. "I - well. Thank you, Miss Voltage. That's very kind of you. But...", I smile sadly at her. "...Things don't always work out that smoothly, right? I don't have my copy of the contract on me here - I couldn't risk losing it, after all - it's in a safe back in my hotel room. If you can escort me back there, I'm happy to show it to you and show you the rest of the evidence I've collected, but, are you able to do so if it means leaving this place unguarded?"

I keep my fingers near my hypnotic wand. I'm almost genuinely willing to give her a chance, but if she tries to call for backup - someone to cover for her here at the theater - I need to stop her immediately and resort to hypnotizing her. I remember her from the show at the Paramount - I never forget a face - and though she didn't volunteer herself, she watched me hypnotize others, which always makes someone a bit more susceptible to being hypnotized by me themselves. Still, a part of me wants to believe in her, and hopes that she doesn't call for backup and is instead just willing to leave this place unguarded, given that she's not very comfortable with the assignment in the first place.

Outcome
-------
Voltage's face shows genuine concern at your words, her brow creasing as she processes the dilemma you've presented. She glances back down the corridor toward the offices, then toward the exit, clearly weighing her options.

"My hotel room's not far," you continue, maintaining that sad but hopeful expression. "Ten minutes there, ten back. You'd have the evidence in hand, properly documented, and we could return here together to search Hutchins's files with everything above board."

She's silent for a long moment, one hand coming up to tap against her silver bracer—a nervous habit, perhaps. The emergency lights cast strange shadows across her face as she thinks.

"Okay," she says finally, and you can hear the mix of determination and uncertainty in her voice. "Okay, here's what we're doing. You're right that I can't just leave this place completely unguarded, but..." She pulls out her phone, and your hand tenses near your pocket. "I'm going to set the motion sensors to alert my communicator instead of just logging locally. If anyone else tries to break in while we're gone, I'll know immediately and we can get back here fast."

She's typing on her phone as she speaks, not calling anyone, just adjusting settings. You relax slightly.

"There," she says, pocketing the device. "The Guardians' tech specialist—Cipher—set up this system for me. It'll ping me if there's any movement inside the building." She looks up at you, and there's something almost vulnerable in her expression. "I'm trusting you here, Ashecroft. I'm trusting that you're telling me the truth, and that this isn't some elaborate setup. Please don't make me regret that."

She moves past you toward the exit, gesturing for you to lead the way. "Your hotel. Show me everything you've got. And then we come back here and do this right."

As you walk toward the stage door, she stays a careful three feet behind you—still cautious, still a hero, but committed now to investigating your claims. The cool night air hits you both as you step outside into the alley.

"Which hotel?" Voltage asks, falling into step beside you as you head toward the street. "And walk me through what else you found. You mentioned other performers getting stiffed. How many? How did you track them down?"

She's trying to build a complete picture, her analytical mind assembling the pieces. Every answer you give will either strengthen her trust or raise new doubts.

Secret Information
------------------
Maya has committed to investigating Victor's claims and is following him to his hotel to see the supposed evidence. She genuinely believes she's made the right ethical choice, though she's aware she's taking a risk trusting him. She hasn't called for backup or informed other Guardians because she doesn't want to seem indecisive or incompetent—part of her inexperience showing. The motion sensor alert is real and will function, but it only covers the interior of the theater. She's maintaining some physical distance and awareness, but her guard is significantly lowered compared to their first encounter. She's vulnerable to hypnotic suggestion now, especially given that she watched Victor's show previously and was fascinated by his hypnosis demonstrations.
